what_this_is: The Workshop rows for tools/plan-my-time: the person's tasks placed into their free time, and their meetings judged against their pursuits; slots proposed for tasks around calendar events by the moved calendar planner; and how a planned task shows on the person's own calendar. None changes a calendar.

payload.label: Plan my time
payload.job: Plan the person's tasks into their free time and judge their meetings against their pursuits, like an auto-scheduling calendar: ASAP first, then hard deadlines, then what serves their most important pursuit, then due date; tasks wait for their blockers, long tasks split into pieces, hard deadlines may use time outside working hours. Returns each task's placed times, whether it fits (on track, past due, will not fit) and when it finishes, and proposes declining meetings that serve no pursuit when they keep more valuable work from meeting its deadline. Changes no calendar; apply the result with the calendar actions. Also reports each day's planned work against a daily cap with which tasks to move to tomorrow first, keeps fixed-time tasks exactly where they are, uses a task's own named schedule (theme days, a pursuit's hours), keeps a gap around work, flags tasks that keep rolling over for a decision, and ignores declined, all-day and free calendar events.
payload.description: Free time is the weekly schedule in the person's time zone, minus busy events, blocks and work already placed. Tasks are placed in this order: a fixed-time task at its exact time, then ASAP, then hard deadlines, then value (the weight of the pursuits it serves times its priority), then due date; a task waits until the tasks that block it end. A task shorter than the rules' first chunk is never split; a longer one is split only into pieces of at least the rules' minimum block. A hard-deadline task that cannot meet its deadline in working hours may use time outside them, and says so. Each task comes back as on_track, past_due, unfit_past_due, unfit_later, needs_decision (it has moved `rolled_over` days in a row), conflict (its fixed time is taken), blocked or not_planned (no length, already done, or a deadline long past), with the words that say why. A meeting that serves no pursuit and is not required is proposed for decline, lowest value first, only while declining it lets more valuable work meet its deadline; nothing is declined here. Each day's planned minutes come back against the rules' daily cap with the lowest-value movable tasks to move first. Every policy number is the rules file's (read-data/rules.json) and any of them can be overridden in the request's `rules`.

now.description: Plan from this time (ISO); now when left out

time_zone.description: The person's time zone, like America/New_York (UTC when left out)

schedule.description: Working hours per weekday: { monday: [{ from: "09:00", to: "17:00" }], ... }

needle_mover.description: The pursuit that matters most; work for it counts for more

schedule.description: Name of a schedule in schedules or rules.schedules

preferred_start.description: Start it at this time when free (ISO)

rigid.description: With preferred_start: only that exact time, else fit conflict

rolled_over.description: Days in a row it has moved to the next day

planned_for.description: Local date (YYYY-MM-DD) it is committed to; counts toward that day's load

rules.description: Overrides for the planning policy (window_days, stale_days, chunks, pursuit_weight, priority_weight, schedule, schedules, gap_minutes, slot_choice, daily_cap_minutes, rollover_alert_at)

schedules.description: Named working hours: { evenings: { monday: [{ from, to }] } }

end_of_day.description: Local date to the time that day's work must end: { "2026-10-19": "15:00" }

provenance.source: An auto-scheduling calendar's placement of tasks into free time and a daily planner's day caps, built 2026-10-15 from reverse engineering and ordered by the person's pursuits

payload.label: Propose slots for tasks around calendar events
payload.job: Propose work-hour slots for my tasks around the events already on my calendar, saying for each task that does not fit exactly why, and writing nothing
payload.description: Give tasks ({ id, title, duration_minutes, due?, deadline_type hard|soft|none?, priority urgent|high|medium|low?, start_on?, blocked_by?, and for a task already placed starts_at, ends_at, auto_placed, pinned_until }), events (busy events: starts_at, ends_at, or all_day/day), options ({ start_day, horizon_days up to 60, working_hours { start_minute, end_minute, weekdays } or { days: [...] } of sorted intervals, slot_minutes, capacity per weekday, day_overrides, blockers }) and time_zone (the IANA zone working hours are in). Deadline type and priority are independent: the type says whether due binds and whether the task may be placed late; priority only ranks. A task an automatic placement put somewhere that a person then moved stays where they put it while its pin is live (kept) and goes back to the planner when the pin passes (released). Answers proposals (task_id, starts_at, ends_at, status scheduled|late), unscheduled (each with the one reason the fixed precedence chooses: previous-stage tasks that cannot fit, then the blocker chain with blocker_ids, else no free slot), kept, released, and days with each day's planned minutes against its capacity (ok, caution, over). Limits: 200 tasks, 3000 events, 60 days. Nothing is written.

provenance.source: moved from Trillion-X/trillion parts/ui/show/schedule-calendar (schedule-planner, schedule-placement, timebox-policy; original code)

payload.label: Say how a planned task shows on my calendar
payload.job: Say whether and how a planned task becomes an event on my own calendar: not at all, as free time, as busy, or busy only when it is at risk or high priority
payload.description: Give policy (off, free, busy or busy_when_at_risk; off when left out), task (title, due, deadline_type, priority), proposal (the placement the planner proposed: starts_at, ends_at, late) and todo_privacy (private or visible). Answers event ({ title, start, end, transparency transparent|opaque, visibility }) exactly at the proposed placement, or null when the policy writes nothing, and policies (each choice with its label and whether it writes). A task is at risk when it was placed after its deadline, or its deadline binds and falls within 48 hours of the placed end. An unknown policy writes nothing. Nothing is written here: the caller puts the event on the calendar.
